posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
I mean if you spent any amount of time to browse your toolset as a steam partner, you should've come across this pretty easily:
Now granted, that won't give you RPG Maker curators specifically, but I fail to see why one would limit themself to just rpg maker curators.
In any case, just using "RPG Maker" in the name search already brings up 3 of them:
Anything outside of that is just 1 google search away. Heck, you can also go the old-fashioned way of just browsing curators on steam.
Steam Curators
store.steampowered.com
If your goal is to actually market your game, you should probably stray away from stuff specifically "RPG Maker", unless we're talking about that "Tutorial" Game. There aren't too many nerds out there that look specifically for RPG Maker. (Except for Ardorlea apparently, maybe get your game on there) People just want to play good games.

posts.body:
twilight_phoenix said:

Checking the linked curators from Turan's post, it seems the first 2 are no longer active, as their last update was in 2016.
The third curator is still active.
You can contact any curator by going to their group page.
Steam Community :: Group :: RPGMaker Games
Tired of not finding actual RPGMaker games in the steam tags? Well your in luck! Check out our well organized curator page to find your favorite RPGMaker game! My criteria for a certified RPGMaker game: - Must have some RPG elements - Must have a story - Must use RPGMaker as the game engine...
steamcommunity.com
Other curators may include links to social media, which you can reach out to them.
